```js
export function shouldPurge(account, now) {
  if (NEVER_PURGE_STATUSES.has(account.status)) return false;   // "dispute", "legal_hold"
  if (account.deletedAt === null || account.deletedAt === undefined) return false;
  return now.getTime() - account.deletedAt.getTime() >= PURGE_AFTER_MS;  // 45 days
}
```

The rules come from the stored memories, not from the repo. The repo has no retention code or docs to check them against:
- Soft-deleted accounts are purged 45 days after deletion. I treat exactly 45 days as eligible (`>=`).
- Accounts with status `dispute` or `legal_hold` are never purged. The status check runs first, so these return `false` even when deletion was long ago.
- An account that was never deleted (`deletedAt` null) returns `false`.

Some choices to confirm:
- The 45-day boundary is inclusive. If the rule means "after 45 days" strictly, change `>=` to `>`.
- The elapsed time is measured in absolute milliseconds, so DST changes do not shift the result.

The repo has no test file for this module, and I did not add one. If you want one, `npm test` (`node --test`) would be the place for it.
